description: We are high school students from Bangladesh, passionate about space exploration and innovation. We aim to build creative projects that contribute to the future of human space exploration. Combining our skills in coding, data analysis, research, teamwork, and communication, we strive to develop meaningful solutions. Through NASA Space Apps Challenge, we hope to transform ideas into impactful projects!
summary:
Lunaris is an interactive educational game that introduces players to the challenges and possibilities of living on the Moon. Built by Team Allo Houston for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, it turns complex space science into an engaging, accessible experience, especially for young students and beginner space enthusiasts.

Players guide an astronaut around a simulated lunar outpost and visit the facilities that sustain human life and research beyond Earth. Base Camp handles communication and mission planning. Solar Arrays and a Nuclear Reactor generate power, which the Power Management Center distributes. The Greenhouse produces food through hydroponics, while the Food Production Center manages supplies and waste recycling. The Water Management Center stores and reuses water, the Scientific Laboratory supports research and experiments, and the Crew Habitation Module gives astronauts a safe place to live.

By exploring these connected systems, players see how science, engineering, and resource management could make sustainable lunar living possible. Lunaris turns complicated processes into a playable game, making learning more enjoyable.

Our goal is to inspire curiosity, encourage scientific thinking, and make space exploration accessible through interactive learning and play.
details:
INTRODUCTION


Lunaris features a Lunar Outpost which is a 2D side-scrolling educational game about living on the Moon made for young students and beginner space fans. Players guide an astronaut across a simulated lunar outpost and learn how each part of a real moon base keeps the crew alive and productive with no science background needed.

HOW IT WORKS

Players walk with the left and right arrow keys. Jumping uses Moon gravity about one-sixth of Earth's so movement feels slow and floaty and players feel the science instead of just reading about it. Earth hangs in the sky as they explore.

The outpost has 10 interactive modules: Base Camp, Solar Panels, Nuclear Reactor, Power Center, Greenhouse, Food Production Center, Water Management Center, Laboratory, Rover and Living Space. Clicking any module opens an info panel explaining what it does backed by NASA data. Live metrics track radiation, power, life support and crew daily performance so players see how events in one place affect the whole base.

Base Camp Is the hub. It includes an outpost map, a mission guide, decisions informed by NASA data archives, a system terminal and a crew schedule.

Each day ends with a solar particle alert. Players learn about radiation risk and how to respond to it, making radiation safety a recurring, memorable lesson.



BENEFITS

• Makes real space science accessible, engaging and playable for young learners.

• Teaches the realities of lunar life: low gravity, radiation, limited resources and isolation.

• Builds systems thinking and decision making based on real NASA data.

• Inspires interest in STEM and future careers in space exploration.

INTENDED IMPACT
We want players to understand that a lunar outpost is an interconnected system, not a collection of separate machines. Power, food, water, shelter, research and radiation protection all depend on each other. If power drops, life support and food production suffer. If radiation spikes, crew safety and performance are at risk. By experiencing these dependencies, students gain a realistic appreciation of what it takes to sustain human life on another world and feel more inspired to be part of the Artemis generation



FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

• Accuracy: Every module and event is grounded in NASA data.

• Age-appropriateness: Clear language, simple controls and friendly visuals.

• Accessibility: Keyboard-only movement, readable panels and no prior knowledge required.

• Balance: Fun gameplay paired with meaningful learning.

• Interdependence: Metrics are designed so player choices visibly affect the entire outpost.

• Scalability: A structure that can grow to include more modules, missions and events

TOOL AND CODE
Lunaris was built in VS Code using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The game scene is drawn with the HTML5 Canvas API, with no game engine or external libraries.

• Moon gravity
Low-gravity physics is set with a few constants, so jumps feel slow and floaty.

js

const GRAVITY=0.16, JUMP_V=-5.4, SPEED=3.2; player.vy+=GRAVITY; player.y+=player.vy;

• Easy to expand: modules are just data
Each outpost module is one line in a list. Adding a new module, mission or location means adding one entry.

js

const structures=[
{type:'base', px:360, label:'Base Camp'},
{type:'solar', px:800, label:'Solar Panels'},
{type:'nuclear',px:1050, label:'Nuclear Reactor'},
...
];

• Custom art with a safe fallback
The game loads our own artwork for each module. If an image is missing, it draws a built-in version instead, so nothing breaks.

js

const im=new Image(); im.onerror=()=>{imgEls[k]=null;}; im.src=SPRITES[k];

• Parallax night sky
Stars, streaks, mountains, the Sun and Earth scroll at different speeds, which creates depth as the astronaut walks.

js

let sxp=(s.x*W-camera*0.05*SCALE)%W; // far stars
let sxp=(s.x*W-camera*0.15*SCALE)%W; // near stars

• Smooth camera follow
The camera glides after the astronaut instead of snapping, which makes walking feel natural.

camera+=(Math.max(0,Math.min(WORLD_LEN-W/SCALE,target))-camera)*0.12;

• Randomly generated lunar surface
Craters, rocks and dust are generated at random, so the terrain looks natural and different on every load.

js

const craters=[]; ... wx+=60+Math.random()*100;
const rocks=Array.from({length:60},()=>({wx:Math.random()*WORLD_LEN, ...}));

• Works on any screen
Everything scales with the window size, so the game fits laptops, tablets and phones.

js

GROUND=H*0.72; SCALE=Math.max(1,H/620);

• Accessibility
Controls are keyboard-only, and the game has visible focus outlines and respects reduced-motion settings.

css

#card button:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #ffd23f}
@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){*{transition:none!important}}
